item.title: GUARD Corrects Missing-Modality Errors in Frozen Multimodal Predictors
item.description:
GUARD Corrects Missing-Modality Errors in Frozen Multimodal Predictors

A new method called GUARD addresses the problem of deployed multimodal predictors encountering missing modalities after their weights are frozen, providing a way to correct errors without changing the original model.

🔍 Overview

  • A deployed multimodal predictor may face missing modalities after its weights can no longer be changed.
  • Training‑time repair does not answer what part of the resulting error is still correctable from the information that remains.
  • The correctable part is characterized by the Bayes gap: the difference between the model’s prediction and the Bayes prediction given the observed modalities.
  • For cross‑entropy and squared error, excess risk measures this gap in the geometry of the loss; ambiguity in the observed modalities cannot be removed.
  • A badly degraded prediction is not necessarily a correctable one.
  • Estimating the Bayes prediction normally requires labels.

🧩 How it works

GUARD leaves the deployed predictor unchanged and operates in three stages:

  1. Retrieval: Estimates a candidate correction by retrieval.
  2. Learning: Learns from deployment‑matched labeled data when correction is likely to help.
  3. Calibration: Calibrates a threshold on a held‑out split by conformal risk control.

⚙️ Key details

  • When a model observing more modalities is conditionally correct, averaging its outputs conditional on the remaining modalities recovers the Bayes target without retrieval labels; with the same fixed blend and neighbors, it is no worse in expected cross‑entropy or Brier risk than averaging hard labels.
  • Some such assumption is unavoidable: otherwise the target is not identifiable from unlabeled data alone.
  • Under exchangeability, the marginal probability that GUARD applies a correction whose loss increase exceeds a prescribed tolerance is bounded by a preset level, regardless of the learned score.

💡 Why it matters

  • In controlled experiments across nine frozen model‑dataset pairs spanning six domains, GUARD retains most of blanket correction’s gain within harm budgets that blanket correction often exceeds.
  • Correction gain follows headroom rather than raw error.

#MultimodalLearning #ConformalPrediction #ModelDeployment #BayesRisk #MachineLearning

Source: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities

item.title: Selective, Risk‑Controlled Forecasting of Conversational Emotion Shifts
item.description:
Selective, Risk‑Controlled Forecasting of Conversational Emotion Shifts

A new paper submitted on 4 Nov 2026 introduces a reformulation of emotion forecasting in conversation, shifting focus from predicting the next emotional state to detecting departures from persistence with conformal risk guarantees.

🔍 Overview

  • Emotion forecasting has been framed as predicting the next emotional state’s value.
  • The authors argue that this target is hard to observe and propose a learnable, deployable reformulation that treats the task as detecting when a speaker’s emotion departs from its recent state.

🧩 How it works

  • Selective departure forecasting – the task is recast with a lead‑time‑weighted metric and a leakage protocol.
  • Commitment policies – different policies are evaluated; the best choice changes depending on the departure rate.
  • Dialogue‑level conformal risk control – bounds the expected loss of predictions that are committed, providing a guarantee across all twelve tested configurations.
  • The guarantee is achieved through abstention; coverage and alarm recall drop sharply on the most difficult corpus.

📊 Findings

  • Repeating a speaker’s own previous state establishes a persistence baseline that no frozen‑encoder correction improves upon, while a state‑space filter exceeds it.
  • The baseline requires the historical state to be observed; an estimated anchor performs worse than a direct forecaster.
  • Timing of departure from persistence is learnable on three of four corpora but near chance on the highest‑base‑rate corpus, a negative result reported.
  • One language model’s confidence fails as a ranking signal, whereas another succeeds; the failure is model‑dependent and not yet linked to model family or scale.

🚀 Availability

  • Code and result logs can be obtained from the corresponding author upon request.

Computer Science > Computation and Language

#EmotionForecasting #ConformalPrediction #ConversationAI

Source: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation: From a Persistence Barrier to Departure Detection with Conformal Guarantees

item.title: New Tail-Aware Geometry Learning Framework for Multivariate Conformal Prediction
item.description:
New Tail-Aware Geometry Learning Framework for Multivariate Conformal Prediction

Researchers have introduced a tail-aware geometry learning framework for conformal ellipsoids to improve uncertainty quantification in multivariate conformal prediction (CP).

🔍 Overview

Multivariate conformal prediction is a distribution-free uncertainty quantification framework providing finite-sample coverage guarantees. This new approach addresses limitations in existing minimum-volume methods, which rely on quantile thresholds that ignore tail residual severity and bind geometry learning to coverage levels.

🧩 How it works

The proposed framework decouples tail sensitivity in geometry learning from the final coverage guarantee using the following process:

  • Two-split design: The system uses an estimation split and a held-out calibration split.
  • Metric matrix learning: The metric matrix is learned via volume minimization under a CVaR constraint on the estimation split.
  • Calibration: Standard conformal calibration is applied to the held-out calibration split.

⚙️ Key details

  • Convexity: The resulting problem is convex.
  • Bounded-reweighting: The method admits a bounded-reweighting interpretation that prioritizes samples with high residuals.
  • Theoretical characterization: The research characterizes the trade-off between ellipsoidal volume and tail severity.
  • Performance: Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

#ConformalPrediction #UncertaintyQuantification #MachineLearning #MultivariateAnalysis

Source: Tail-Aware Geometry Learning for Conformal Ellipsoids
